svg.aria-label: so the checkpoint interval IS the at-least-once error bound
svg.text: Barrier alignment, and three recoveries from one crash
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = which group it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the keys state is held per. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: CHK — the index the checkpoint in this chapter was taken at. CHK = 4
13 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
15 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
16 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest event time through i, minus LAG.
23 // primitive: barrierIndex(k) — the index at which source k injects its barrier.
25 // primitive: PREFIX_V — the v already in the checkpoint. PREFIX_V = 23
26 // primitive: SUFFIX_V — the v after it. SUFFIX_V = 22
28 // function: align() — the stage snapshots only when the barrier has arrived from
29 // EVERY source, buffering anything that overtakes its own barrier meanwhile.
43 // function: recover(hasState, offset) — resume with or without each half of the
44 // checkpoint. Only the matching pair reaches the no-crash total.
49 for (i in offset + 1 .. len(EVENTS) - 1) { total = total + EVENTS[i].v }
55 // function: errorBound(k) — under at-least-once, how much can be double counted
56 // when checkpointing every k events? It is the checkpoint interval, in v.
63 for (j in i - since + 1 .. i) { run = run + EVENTS[j].v }
69 // function: main() — THE CALLER: alignment, three recoveries, one bound.
Step 4/0 — so the checkpoint interval IS the at-least-once error bound
`errorBound` sums the v of the events since the last checkpoint and keeps the largest — 12 at k = 3. Note what it takes as its only argument: `k`. The interval
chosen in the previous concept for I/O and recovery time also sets how wrong an at-least-once answer can be.
